newsitem.title: USA: White House backs proposed rollback of SEC fees.
newsitem.headline: White House backs proposed rollback of SEC fees.

text.p: The Clinton administration supports a proposed $850 million, 10-year fee rollback for the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, a spokesman for the Office of Mangement and Budget said Tuesday.
"We support the proposal," said Larry Haas, associate director for communications for the OMB.

The proposal rollback was agreed to Monday night by the House Commerce Committee chairman, Rep. Thomas Bliley, a Virginia Republican, and Sen. Fritz Hollings, the South Carolina Democrat who leads Senate conferees reconciling House and Senate versions of a bill designed to deregulate the U.S. securities industry.
The House version of the bill had originally called for a $700 million fee rollback over five years.
The proposal is part of a scheme to allow the SEC to be less reliant on fees for its funding.
Under the plan, Congress would include the SEC in the normal budgetary process in a move to minimize snags when its funding comes up for congressional approval each year.
The OMB had opposed the rollback initially, noting that under the proposed budget scheme, the SEC would have to compete with other agencies for funding.
Haas did not say why the OMB had changed its stand. But he said the budget office now would "do everything we can to be helpful" in getting the bill passed.
"It's our hope that we can get it done," he said. The current congressional term adjourns September 27.
An SEC spokeswoman said the agency had no comment on fee proposal.
The fee rollback is a crucial issue that has stalled consideration of the securities bill, which seeks to eliminate duplicative regulations enforced by the SEC and state regulators.
It will also give the SEC more powers to regulate and lessen the role of the states in overseeing the mutual fund industry.
